start_here: Say to your AI: "Show me whether every copy of my things is in step, and which records two of my devices changed apart", with {"thing_type":"note"}. It runs tool:see-if-my-copies-are-in-step and answers {"devices":[],"versions":[],"other_kinds":[]}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours and keeps nothing: the device rows, the records kept apart and the records they name come in with the request.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Show me whether every copy of my things is in step, and which records two of my devices changed apart", and give it thing_type (The kind of record whose versions to read or settle (one kind per call; other_kinds names the rest)).
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:see-if-my-copies-are-in-step and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Reads and changes nothing: the device rows, the records kept apart and the records they name come in with the request. Answers devices (each device's state, waiting changes and when it last caught up; a copy of your records you send in positions is shown once, as the device that named it or as a copy of its own) and versions (each record kept apart of the kind you name as thing_type: the record as it is now first, then one side per other version, with the words of its keep button). other_kinds names the kinds of other records kept apart, to ask about next.
4. It reads and writes no rows: everything it works from is in the request.
